contracts.rule: Authored `artNotes` are appended to what a builder derived, entity note first and the narrower rung second, and an empty note adds nothing, so a project that authors no notes composes byte-identical prompts. A shot's prompt reads only the shot's own notes.
contracts.prevents: Re-keying every task in every project that authors no notes, and losing the style preamble, reference scaffolding and closing frame clause that keep a picture on-model, which a replaced prompt would drop.
contracts.detail: `artNotes` is an optional free-text field at five rungs: `Character`, `Location`, `Shot`, each `Outfit` and each `LocationVariant`. Setting a note costs money by design, like an outfit and unlike a scene edit: the note is in the prompt, so it re-keys exactly the tasks its rung reaches. `buildShotPrompt` leaves out the entity notes because they already reach the frame through the plates and sheets it references. The test worth having is the byte-identical output of a project with no notes, not the feature. Where the notes, seeds and image models are written is `prompts.artRungsShared`, in `@vn/artgen`.

contracts.rule: Art notes, image seeds and image models are authored at the same five rungs, addressed as `character:<id>[/<outfit>]`, `location:<id>[/<variant>]` or `shot:<sceneId>/<shotId>`, and every host writes them through one parser and one write path, with the same refusals.
contracts.prevents: Two hosts drifting into two rung vocabularies, so the agent and the desktop refuse or write the same authorial act differently, or create the outfit, variant or shot a typo named.
contracts.detail: An entity rung is written into the sheet the model was built from, through `@vn/model`'s `apply*Edit`; a shot rung into `work/shots/<sceneId>.json`. An empty value clears the rung back to inheriting. The narrowest seed wins (`seedFor`) and is in the task hash; the narrowest image model wins (`modelFor`) and is outside it, and a slot a generation graph binds takes the graph node's own model and seed instead. The Wiki pane's sheet form is a second writer of the same keys (`art_notes`, `seed`, `image_model`) through `@vn/parse`'s front-matter codec, because the `art.*` commands re-serialise the whole front matter and lose the author's comments; the model reads the keys back identically, and a blank box removes the key. `regenerate_asset` is always confirm-gated and refuses where the host has no pipeline (vnauthor). The agent reads a rendered picture back through `view_image` (`describeAsset`, a plain vision question rather than the P7 reviewer).

contracts.rule: A derived prompt is a `PromptChunk[]` of keyed clauses, which `renderPrompt` collapses to the flat string a task hashes. An override edits that list at the one rung naming the whole picture, and a project with no override composes byte-identical prompts.
contracts.prevents: Every existing task re-keying, and so every picture re-rendering, when prompts became editable; and an agent-condensed prompt re-rendering its asset because an unrelated note moved a clause under it.
contracts.detail: Every builder in `@vn/stills` assembles the list. Each clause is keyed, categorised, and carries an origin (a builder, or the document and field its sentence came from) that a surface can open. `renderPrompt` is the `.filter(Boolean).join(' ')` tail the flat builders ended with, and `prompthash.test.ts` pins the sorted hash list against a literal written before chunks existed. The override rungs are `Character` for a portrait, the outfit entry for a sheet, the location variant for a plate and the `Shot` for a frame, never a rung that only contributes a clause, so there is one place to look. Setting `mode` alone overrides nothing: every mode falls back to the derived chunks when the shape it names is empty, and each writer calls `promptOverrideIsEmpty` to clear the key. `TaskInputs.*.prompt` stays a flat string, because `taskHash` hashes the whole inputs object with no allow-list; a chunk reaches a hash only through `composePrompt`'s text. An override edit re-keys exactly the tasks its rung reaches, as an art note does. An agent-condensed prompt records the chunk list it condensed (`chunkFingerprint`). When those chunks move, `composePrompt` in `agent` mode still returns the stored text and reports `held`, and never falls back to fresh chunks; the staleness is derived on read and shown on the pane, never stored.

contracts.rule: P5 receives the scene as identified lines, `[<lineId>] <kind>/<speaker>: <text>`, never as flattened prose, and a decomposition that binds none of the scene's real line ids falls back to the baseline.
contracts.prevents: A model copying an empty `"coversLines":[]` from the response template, which produces shots that are drawn and never displayed, because the exporter shows a shot only where its lines are.
contracts.detail: The system prompt asks the model to assign every line to exactly one shot, in order; the code does not enforce that, and a line the answer leaves uncovered stays uncovered. What the code enforces: line ids the scene does not have are dropped, a decomposition that binds no real line falls back to the baseline (`withCoverage`), and an uncovered first line goes to the first shot, so a scene cannot open on a blank frame. `coversLines` is not in a frame's task inputs, so these repairs re-key nothing.

contracts.rule: A storyboard is single frames or manga pages, as `shot_form` decides. A page's panels carry their own cast, drawn from the shot's, and their own lettered lines. Under `lettering: model` those lines are in the page's prompt and hash; a panel's bubbles are in no prompt.
contracts.prevents: Storyboard notes or an art style turning frames into pages on their own, a panel casting someone no sheet was drawn for, a lettered page's redraw left out of a coverage edit's price, and a bubble placement re-rendering the page it sits on.
contracts.detail: `shot_form` (`frames`, the default, or `pages`) decides whether a new storyboard is single frames or manga pages of panels. Under `pages`, `decompSystem` tells the model to make every shot a page and adds the page vocabulary: the layout template names with their panel counts, the camera vocabulary and the `MAX_PANELS` bound. Under `frames` it adds none of that, whatever the art style or the notes say, so the notes cannot turn frames into pages on their own. Storyboard notes add the staging-sheet paragraph, and either `pages` or notes brings the wider answer format, whose optional `panels?` key is then the only mention of panels in the prompt's own text. The agent's `propose_storyboard` reads the same field and takes a `form` argument that overrides it for one scene, to be passed only when the author explicitly asks for the other form. The desktop writes the field through `project.setShotForm`, a dropdown on the Project pane. A shot with `panels` is a page: one image of several panels, each with an outline in page fractions, its own framing, camera and cast, and the lines it letters. `readShots` refuses a file whose panel casts someone outside the shot's `subjects`, with `panel_subject_not_in_cast`. A covered line no panel letters comes back in `LoadedShots.unpanelled`, the planner logs it as a `line_in_no_panel` warning, `setPanels` names it in its message, and the page still renders. A page's prompt is built by `buildPageChunks`, which `buildShotChunks` calls for a shot with panels. Under `lettering: model` the lettered lines are in the prompt verbatim, so the text and its panel assignment are in the task hash: a coverage take on a page, or a line edit inside one, re-keys the page. Every host's coverage take says so through `letteredPagesNote` in `@vn/scriptedit`. `lettering` defaults to `runner`, which draws the page wordless, because the manga plan's Stage 2 live check found the default image model unfit for lettering and only the expensive ones fit; a project that wants the model to letter says so. A panel's `bubbles` (`PanelBubble`: the line, an anchor, an optional tail and an optional name flag, in page fractions) are authored and outside the prompt: no builder reads them, so `story.setBubbles` and the agent's `set_bubbles` (one rule, `setBubbles` in `@vn/scriptedit`) re-key nothing. `set_bubbles` is defined and exported, but `ALL_TOOLS` does not list it, so the agent's registry does not offer it. `setBubbles` refuses a frame, a line no panel letters, a line named twice and a point off the page. A bubble's line must be one its panel letters: `readShots` drops a bubble whose line left the panel, and `setPanels` drops one whose line it moved to another panel, since the anchor was placed against the old one. The exporter (`buildPlayable`) copies bubbles into the playable only under `lettering: runner`. `shotData.panelBoxes` holds the panel boxes a reviewer measured on the image the shot holds (a `done` output, or a `needs_human` shot's last attempt), from `DefectReport.observed`, which the review fills only for a page. It is derived, like `proseHash`: the planner stamps it only with new image bytes, so a rerun that reports the same image leaves it alone. The runner's `layoutReport` matches every measuring reviewer's boxes against the intended outlines (`matchPanels`, IoU at or above `LAYOUT_IOU`) and files a `layout` defect of its own only when none of them match, because a reviewer's measurement can be off while none invents a match for a wrong page; a page no reviewer measured gets no layout verdict. The boxes stamped are the matching reviewer's, or the first reviewer's when none matched.

contracts.rule: A reference is a `ChunkRef` on one clause: muting the clause drops it, the task hashes its `pin` rather than its slot, authored refs follow the derived ones in `TaskInputs.refs`, and a ref with no `from` names an asset by hash and never drifts.
contracts.prevents: An upstream approval silently re-rendering everything that points at it, a muted clause still feeding the model its pictures, and every task with no authored reference re-keying, since `canonicalJson` maps arrays by position.
contracts.detail: A linked ref carries a `RefBinding` naming the slot it was taken from (`plate:cafe/night`, `sheet:aiko/gala/front`). Drift is `resolveBinding(from) !== pin`, derived on read, and a slot that cannot be resolved reports none; a moved slot suspends what was pinned to its old hash rather than re-rendering it. `prompt.addRef` attaches a bare asset hash with no `from`, because an upload or a concept has no slot under it. `applyPromptEdit` refuses a reference on a clause the prompt does not have, and the same pin twice on one clause, since `refs` is positional and inside the hash. The cycle refusal is `prompts.refsAcyclic`.

contracts.rule: The reference graph over slots stays acyclic: `prompt.addRef` runs `refCycle` in its check and refuses a reference that would close a loop, naming the whole path. The cycle is over slots, not hashes.
contracts.prevents: Tasks that are never ready, because each waits on the other, so a run appears to do nothing and reports no error.
contracts.detail: Hashes cannot cycle, but bindings can: "Aiko's portrait references Aiko's gala sheet" closes a loop although no hash repeats, because the sheet's prompt already references the portrait. A ref cycle is invisible to `topoOrder`, which reads `Task.deps`. Left unchecked, `doneOutput` answers `undefined`, the shot is skipped, and the plan-run-replan loop starves in silence. `firstCycle` finds a loop already on disk in a hand-edited project, and the planner calls it so such a project fails loudly.

contracts.rule: The P7 reviewer sees only what `shotSpec` says about the shot: its own framing, location and cast, with the prose of its covered lines marked as context only. `spec.characters` decides who must be in frame, and an empty list means an absence is not a defect.
contracts.prevents: A reviewer handed the scene synopsis flagging every shot, plates included, for characters the scene mentions but the shot never ordered, so the refine loop spends every attempt and lands on `needs_human`.
contracts.detail: `Shot.castOptional` exempts a shot that has a cast from the same trap: the subjects stay on the shot, so their sheets still reach the generator as references, but `shotSpec` hands the reviewer an empty `characters` and the description says an absence is not a defect. Without it, a frame the reviewer will never accept (a figure seen from behind, a crowd, a hand) spends the whole cap. `story.requireCast` writes the field, normally from the Shot Coverage strip. `shotSpec`'s output never enters a task's `inputs`, and `castOptional` is read only by `shotSpec`, so neither re-keys the shot: setting the field changes what the next review asks and does not by itself redraw the frame.
